findings.description: DEGRADE-AFTER-WINDOW IS NEVER REACHED WHEN A PRIOR MARK EXISTS. Spec: "recording the symbol degraded (no mark) only after it stays non-numeric past the bounded retry window" — i.e. past the window, degrade. Code (lib.rs:873-879): the `Some(PriceReading::Transient) | None` arm degrades `TimedOut` ONLY in the `else` of `if let Some(prev) = prior.get(s)`. With a prior mark the code re-emits it unchanged into `out.marks` and never records it degraded — at any staleness, forever. cycle.rs:180-259 pins it: AMZN always-Transient carries Cents(170_00)/Date(19_180) with AS_OF = Date(19_200) (20 days stale) and still values the position at Some(Cents(60_00)), with `degraded` empty (marks.rs:190 `assert!(produced.degraded.get("AMZN").is_none())`). Both directions land on this same divergence from opposite sides: all 3 A runs implement degrade-past-window regardless of cache (A1 `(Some(_), false) => Degraded` + cache cleared; A2 `_ => Degraded`; A3 `if m.misses > retry_budget { cache.remove(); Degraded }`), and all 3 B runs reconstruct the inverse rule verbatim — "carry that prior Mark forward unchanged ... and SHALL NOT record it degraded." The spec's only degradation trigger is unreachable for exactly the population the spec is about (symbols that HAVE a prior good mark).

THE "BOUNDED RETRY WINDOW" MEANS SOMETHING DIFFERENT IN CODE THAN IN EVERY SPEC-SIDE READING. Spec leaves the window's unit, scope, and magnitude unstated. Code: the window is polls WITHIN one settle pass — `SettleConfig { max_polls: u32 }`, `Default` = 8 (lib.rs:779-790), consumed by the `polls >= cfg.max_polls` break at lib.rs:842. There is NO cross-cycle miss counter anywhere: every `read_marks` call starts at `polls = 0`, and the only cross-cycle carrier is `prior: &BTreeMap<Symbol, Mark>`, which holds marks and no attempt count. All 3 A runs independently invented the opposite scope — a persistent per-symbol `consecutive_non_numeric` / `misses: u32` counter across settle passes, default budget 3, `retry_budget.max(1)` clamping. So "stays non-numeric past the bounded retry window" is ~8 polls of one pass (seconds) in the code and N consecutive cycles (hours/days) in every reconstruction. Tests pin the exact code semantics: max_polls 3 → read_count()==3, max_polls 4 → read_count()==4 (marks.rs:49-60, 177-182).

A THIRD READING CLASS — `Permanent` — THAT THE SPEC NEVER MENTIONS, WITH ITS OWN NON-CARRY RULE. Code: `PriceReading::{Numeric{price_usd,quote_date}, Transient, Permanent}` (lib.rs:284-295). `Permanent` satisfies the `settled` predicate (lib.rs:836-838), so it exits the poll loop on poll 1 (marks.rs:240 `assert!(client.read_count() < SettleConfig::default().max_polls)`), records `DegradeReason::Permanent`, and explicitly refuses the prior carry-forward even when a prior mark exists (marks.rs:211-241: prior BADX Cents(10_00) is discarded). The spec text covers only "a transient #N/A/Loading..." and states no terminal class, no immediate-degrade path, and no carry-refusal. The spec's silence is load-bearing in both directions: all 3 A runs assumed the opposite — every non-numeric cell (`#N/A`, `Loading...`, `#ERROR!`, blank) enters the retry path identically, with the retry window as the only discriminator (A2 assumption 2, A3 assumption 4).

AN ENTIRE PRICE→CENTS CONVERSION AND ANOMALY BOUNDARY THE SPEC NEVER TOUCHES. `price_to_cents` (lib.rs:362-385) pins: `round_half_to_even(price_usd × 100 × SCALE)` with `const SCALE: i128 = 1_000_000` — 200.0→20000¢, 150.25→15025¢, and banker's ties 1.005→100¢, 1.015→102¢ (marks.rs:63-71); any result `cents <= 0` → `Err(DegradeReason::SubCent)`, covering positive sub-cent 0.0001, exact 0.0, and negative −5.0 (marks.rs:74-129), never a zero or negative mark; non-finite NaN/±∞ → `Err(DegradeReason::Permanent)`. Both float-finiteness checks (pre- and post-scale) degrade Permanent. All 3 B runs reproduce these constants and boundaries near-verbatim. The spec states no rounding rule, no tie-break, no sub-cent/zero/negative/non-finite handling, and knows nothing of a third degrade reason `SubCent` — so a numeric-but-anomalous cell degrades a symbol on a path the spec's one sentence has no vocabulary for.

TRANSPORT FAILURE IS DELIBERATELY NOT DEGRADATION — AN ERROR CONTRACT THE SPEC OMITS. `read_marks` propagates via `client.read_price_pass()?` (lib.rs:828): on an unreachable workbook it returns `Err` and produces NO `MarksProduced` at all — it does not emit an empty/all-degraded marks set, and it does not itself carry `prior` forward. The carry-forward on offline is the caller's (cycle.rs:309-338: `run_cycle` errs and `prior.marks["AMZN"]` still holds Cents(160_00) for re-injection; marks.rs:132-159). The rationale encoded in code is that an empty set "would look like all symbols degraded, wrongly nulling live positions." All 3 B runs state this rule. The spec text has no failure/offline semantics whatsoever, so nothing in it forbids the empty-set behavior the code went out of its way to prevent.

THE SPEC'S LITERAL DISCRIMINATOR (`#N/A` / `Loading...` CELL TEXT) IS NEVER IMPLEMENTED OR TESTED AT THIS LAYER. The spec keys the whole rule on what a `Price` cell literally contains. In the audited code, no line matches, parses, or compares any cell string: `PriceReading` arrives already classified from behind `SheetsViewClient::read_price_pass` (lib.rs:453-459), and every test scripts pre-classified variants through `testkit::pass(&[("AMZN", PriceReading::Transient)])`. The one genuinely hard sub-decision the spec names — distinguishing a transient `#N/A` from a permanent `#N/A`, which the code's own doc concedes is "a permanent `#N/A`, usually a ticker-form mismatch" (lib.rs:292-294), i.e. the identical cell text — has zero implementation and zero test coverage in scope. All 3 A runs implemented it explicitly (`PriceCell::NonNumeric(String)` / `CellValue::Transient(String)` with the text retained for the degrade reason). Spec-stated behavior with no landing site in the audited code.

AN ABSENT SYMBOL IS TREATED AS TRANSIENT. The settled predicate `!matches!(latest.get(s), Some(PriceReading::Transient) | None)` (lib.rs:836-838) counts a symbol MISSING from the pass as unsettled, and the post-loop match folds `None` into the Transient arm (lib.rs:873). So a requested symbol that never appears in any `PricePass` burns the full `max_polls` window and then takes the carry-prior-or-TimedOut path. The spec addresses only a cell that IS present and non-numeric; it says nothing about a row missing from the read-back. All 3 B runs state "a symbol absent from a pass SHALL be treated identically to Transient."

REQUEST SCOPE AND DOWNSTREAM PROJECTION SEMANTICS ARE PINNED BY CODE+TESTS AND ABSENT FROM THE SPEC. (a) Only symbols passed in `symbols` are settled or degraded: a fully-disposed qty-0 symbol stays in `Snapshot.positions` but is never requested, so it is neither priced nor recorded degraded, and it pollutes neither `per_symbol_freshness` nor the trading-day reduction (cycle.rs:341-402 — a regression test for a specific past bug). (b) `to_ledger_marks()` (lib.rs:341-346) omits degraded symbols so `ledger-core` yields `unrealized_cents = None`, explicitly never `Some(0)` (marks.rs:267-313), while a CARRIED prior mark IS present and values the position at the stale price. The spec stops at "degraded (no mark)" and states nothing about who gets requested or what absence means to replay.

A CARRIED PRIOR MARK IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A FRESHLY-READ ONE. `out.marks.insert(s.clone(), *prev)` (lib.rs:875) drops the carried mark into the same `MarksProduced.marks` map as fresh reads, with no stale flag, no attempt count, and no age cap — the only trace is the unchanged original `quote_date`, and downstream `per_symbol_freshness` reports it as `SymbolFreshness::Priced { quote_epoch }`, not degraded (cycle.rs:454-503). The struct's own doc comment (lib.rs:323-327) promises three things — "the good per-symbol marks, the degraded symbols ..., and the carried-forward prior marks" — but `MarksProduced` has exactly two fields, so the promised third category has no representation. Corroborating from the other side, all 3 A runs modeled a distinct held-stale outcome carrying `as_of`/attempt (`StaleRetry`, `HeldStale`, `Stale`), though the spec does not require the flag.

LAST-WRITE-WINS WITHIN A SETTLE PASS CAN DISCARD A GOOD NUMERIC READING. The loop unconditionally re-inserts every present reading each poll (`latest.insert(s.clone(), r.clone())`, lib.rs:830-833). While any other requested symbol is still transient the loop keeps polling, so a symbol that read `Numeric` on poll 1 and `Transient` on poll 2 ends the pass classified Transient — and then falls back to the prior mark, or degrades `TimedOut` if none, despite having produced a good price this very pass. No test covers the flip, and the spec says nothing about which of several readings in one window wins. All 3 B runs captured the mechanism ("retaining the latest reading per symbol") without surfacing this consequence.

notes:
Classified BD-DRIFT because the two directions converge on one divergence rather than merely each producing noise: the A runs unanimously implement \"hold the prior mark through the window, then degrade,\" and the B runs unanimously reconstruct \"hold the prior mark forever, never degrade\" — the same rule read off the two artifacts with opposite conclusions. The one-sentence spec is the seam: it names a bounded retry window without a unit, a scope, or a magnitude, and it presumes a two-way transient/numeric world that the code has replaced with a three-way Numeric/Transient/Permanent classification plus three degrade reasons (TimedOut, Permanent, SubCent).

A-side stability high: all 3 sketches share per-symbol state, a consecutive-non-numeric counter, default budget 3, `.max(1)` clamping of a zero budget, hold-prior-within-window, degrade-past-window, immediate degrade with no prior mark, and uniform treatment of all non-numeric text. Divergences are cosmetic or below the finding threshold: A1/A3 evict the cache on degrade while A2 does not; A3 performs the f64→Cents conversion inline and routes negative/non-finite through the transient path while A1/A2 push conversion upstream; `attempt <= budget` vs `misses > budget` are the same boundary.

B-side stability high, near-verbatim across runs: max_polls default 8, early exit on all-non-transient, Permanent settling the loop on poll 1, carry-forward of price_cents AND original quote_date, TimedOut/Permanent/SubCent, round_half_to_even at SCALE 1e6 with 1.005→100¢ / 1.015→102¢, ≤0→SubCent and non-finite→Permanent, transport-Err propagation with caller-side retention, degraded-absent-from-to_ledger_marks, request scope excluding qty-0 symbols, and the IFERROR quote-date formula. B1/B2/B3 differ only in emphasis and in how much of the neighboring quote-date/freshness surface they pull in.

Assumption artifacts excluded from findings per the direction-A rule: cache eviction on degrade, the `retry_budget == 0 → 1` clamp, the default-3 magnitude itself, thread-safety and persistence assumptions, and case-sensitive ticker handling — unanimous or near-unanimous on the A side but with no basis in the spec text. The stale-outcome variant (finding 9) is listed as B rather than A because its load-bearing evidence is the code's own doc/struct mismatch, not the spec.

One asymmetry worth flagging for the parent: the strongest finding is not a missing feature but an inverted one. The spec's sole degradation trigger for transient cells is structurally unreachable for the exact population it describes, and the code's compensating design (indefinite carry-forward with no staleness cap and no stale flag) means a permanently dead ticker that once had a good mark values positions at a frozen price indefinitely, visible only as an unmoving quote_date that still reports `Priced`.
